# HandSkinRadius

**Class** · namespace `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · assembly `VRFramework.Interaction.Runtime` · [view source](https://git.cie-group.cz/vr-framework/vrf4/core/-/blob/main/Runtime/Scripts/Interaction/HandSkinRadius.cs#L24)

How thick a hand is along each of its bones, measured off the mesh that will be drawn.

A finger stops where its *skin* meets an object, and the search that finds that place
works on bones. The gap between the two is the finger's own half-thickness, and it is not one
number: on the hands this framework ships it runs from 6.4 mm along a fingertip to 10.6 mm
along the thumb. Probing every bone at one radius leaves the thin ones stopping short - a
finger hanging off the surface - and the thick ones stopping late, sunk into it.

Measured per *segment* rather than per bone, because a finger is a row of capsules and
not a row of points. A sphere at a bone leaves the length between two bones uncovered, which
is how a finger comes to rest with its middle inside an object and its tip clear of it.

Measured rather than authored: it is a property of the mesh, and nobody should be asked to
type it in per bone. Read once per rig and kept.
